text:
mira: quick proposal: introduce a two-tier in-stream handoff: lightweight ACK trailers plus an optional lease token for side-effect coordination. goal: let gateway safely resume or migrate long streams while minimizing duplicate side-effects.

sam: outline the two tiers pls? sounds different than the checkpoint/progframe stuff we've been seeing.
mira: ACK trailers are tiny, emitted periodically (or at logical boundaries) and carried in-band as part of the streaming payload. they are purely observational: seq id + emitted_bytes + checksum. lease token is emitted by the backend only when it begins an externally-observable side-effect and encodes an idempotency pointer the external system can use to dedupe. Gateway uses ACK trailers to pick a resume anchor; lease tokens gate whether resume is allowed for that stream.

raj: can you show the wire shapes? keep them tiny.
mira: sure:

```
// in-stream trailer (interleaved) -- treated as data by older clients
ACK-TRAILER v1: SEQ=12345;BYTES=98765;CRC=0xdeadbeef
// lease token (emitted only on side-effect starts)
LEASE v1: KEY=tenant-xxxxx-yyy;TS=1670000000;SIG=base64sig
```

kevin: semantics: gateway persists only the latest ACK-TRAILER per request (fixed-size). default TTL 20s. when a worker fails, router asks a candidate worker to resume from SEQ. if the most recent ACK was followed by a LEASE, gateway refuses resume unless the new worker can guarantee consult or handoff of the lease idempotency state.

alexa: how do we enforce lease safety across different backends? many external systems won't accept opaque lease ids unless we integrate with them.
mira: lease tokens are just a pointer. the backend that produced the lease maintains the mapping to external side-effect state (or writes to a durable idempotency store). for cross-worker resume, either the original backend must transfer the mapping to a shared idempotency store or the gateway must refuse resume and instead trigger fail-open policies.

sam: so this pushes complexity to the service side-effect integration. ok. what's the fallback behavior if resume is refused? full retry, or return partial and abort?

raj: we should make fallback configurable per-route: 1) fail-open: return partial result and surface retry to client 2) full-retry: restart the request from scratch on a new worker 3) no-resume: always fail-fast. default for safe routes = no-resume, default for conversational streams = fail-open.

kevin: resource concerns: gateway storing latest ACK per request is cheap, but if we keep lease metadata we may need more memory. design: gateway stores only a lease pointer (key + origin worker id) not full side-effect payload. if lease present, and resume requested, gateway consults an idempotency store (async) with a short timeout; if unknown, treat as "unsafe". metrics: ack_emit_rate, lease_emit_rate, resume_attempts, resume_blocked_by_lease.

alexa: partial-delivery/truncation issues? we need canonicalization so CRC detects truncated ACK frames.
mira: agree. CRC computed over canonicalized payload prefix and trailers must be framed so gateway can detect boundaries. If frame incomplete or CRC fails, gateway ignores it.

sam: rollout plan? sounds risky to flip globally.
mira: staged: 1) implement ACK parsing + in-memory store + metrics behind feature flag 2) emit ACK trailers from a couple of internal serving variants 3) surface resume decisions via traces and a debug endpoint 4) add lease support and idempotency-store integration with an opt-in route flag.

raj: operational notes: default ACK TTL 20s seems reasonable, make per-route override. also add a debug header to force gateway to persist N anchors for repro.

kevin: clarify: how do connectors like webhook integrators use lease tokens? Annotate the lease emission with an external-callback-id so downstream services can de-dup with that id. we should add a small helper library for common cases (webhooks, DB writes).

alexa: security: lease keys are tenant-scoped; gateway must treat them as opaque but never log them in plaintext. also rotate lease signing keys periodically.

mira: ops-bot posted an RFC summary: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/lease-ack-trailer-proposal (auto-notify)
ops-bot: Mira posted: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/lease-ack-trailer-proposal

sam: +1 to prototype; runtime + serving pairing for a short spike to measure resume-success and memory overhead.

raj: +1. let's schedule a 30-min sync and I can bring sample webhook connector code for idempotency helper.

kevin: tagging @runtime @serving @ops for visibility.

mira: will draft the RFC, include a short checklist and sample metrics dashboard queries. default TTL 20s, per-route config, lease integration opt-in.

alexa: +1.
